subject: china-studies
title: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades

questions.prompt: A student says: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the farmland is cleared and the city is built in a single step

Urbanisation is gradual and driven by people moving in: factories and housing are built on farmland at the edge stage by stage, the built-up districts spread outward, and the urban share climbs at every stage.
The city grows only when the government redraws its boundary to include the farmland
The farmland stays the same size and the city grows upward only, so the shares never change

questions.misconception: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once. In fact urbanisation is gradual: factories and the first housing blocks are built on farmland at the edge as migrants arrive for jobs, the districts then spread outward stage by stage, and the urban share climbs 15 to 38 to 62 to 85 while the rural share falls at every stage.

questions.prompt: What is built first at the town edge in stage 2 of the animation?

choices.text: A ring of tall housing blocks around the whole farmland
Factories on farmland at the edge, whose jobs pull people in, with the first housing blocks rising beside them
A new city centre that replaces the small town in one step
Nothing is built - the town boundary is simply redrawn

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: factories are built on farmland at the edge, their jobs pull people in from the countryside, and the first housing blocks rise beside them.

questions.prompt: The urban share is 38 of every 100 people at stage 2 and 62 at stage 3. State the rural share at each stage and explain why it changes.
questions.answer: The rural share is 62 of every 100 at stage 2 and 38 at stage 3: the two shares add to 100, and as built-up districts spread outward and more people live in the city, the urban share climbs and the rural share falls by the same amount.
questions.explanation: Scenes 2 and 3 run this: the urban share climbs 38 to 62 while the rural share falls 62 to 38.

questions.prompt: Explain why the farmland shrinks stage by stage in the animation instead of disappearing at once.
questions.answer: Each stage builds on farmland at the edge of what is already built - factories and first housing in stage 2, then districts spreading outward in stage 3 - so the farmland is used up a strip at a time as people move in, leaving a strip in the west at stage 3 and only a remnant at stage 4.
questions.explanation: The farmland shrinks in s2 and s3 and is a remnant in s4: one stage of building at a time.

questions.prompt: At the final stage, what are the urban and rural shares?

choices.text: Urban 85 and rural 15 of every 100 people
Urban 62 and rural 38 of every 100 people
Urban 100 and rural 0 of every 100 people
Urban 50 and rural 50 of every 100 people

questions.explanation: Scene 4 works this: the city is mostly built-up, with 85 of every 100 people in urban districts and a rural share of 15.
